function.description: Execute a REAL bridge. SPENDS REAL FUNDS AND IS IRREVERSIBLE: it signs and broadcasts a deposit from the user's wallet on the source chain. APPROVAL: over MCP in a restricted project the call WAITS until the user answers the card in Vex, and that card IS the confirmation - do not ask for another in chat. It returns the settled outcome: executed (reported as this tool's own status, confirmed or confirmed_unrecorded), declined, expired, refused, dispatch_failed or indeterminate; never call it twice while you wait and never retry an indeterminate one. In a full project it executes directly under the user's standing permission. Run BridgeQuote first. That quote authorizes THIS tool whichever venue it chose; BridgeQuoteRelay authorizes only BridgeExecuteRelay, and each namespaced khalani__/relay__ execute takes its own pair's quote. PRECONDITIONS, each refused BY NAME: a fresh BridgeQuote on the SAME provider with identical params, within 15 minutes; fromToken/toToken resolved with TokenFind; `amountRaw` in RAW base units at that token's decimals. The route, the refund address and the destination are derived from the source and the selected destination wallet; no parameter can redirect them: a caller-supplied `refundTo`, `referrer`, `referrerFeeBps`, `routeId`, `depositMethod` or `recipient` is rejected by name. `fromAddress` redirects nothing either: the session wallet signs only for itself. Venue comes from Khalani's live chain registry: Khalani when it serves both sides, Relay otherwise, which is how Robinhood Chain routes. Vex charges 25 bps of the input token as a SEPARATE transfer after the deposit lands; a bridge that never happens is never charged. RETURNS status, summary and the fields named in the result. IT NEVER REPORTS SUCCESS: a broadcast deposit is not a delivered bridge. `status` is pending, filled_unverified, failed or refunded, and every arm says do NOT re-bridge. Full contract: vex_ToolDescribe.
function.name: BridgeExecute

amountRaw.description: Amount in raw atomic units of fromToken (e.g. USDC has 6 decimals, so 1 USDC = "1000000"). Get the token's decimals from TokenFind / khalani.tokens.search, which returns decimals per chain - a raw amount next to a token whose decimals you have not read is a thousandfold error waiting to happen.
